description: Creates a new appointment booking on a previously fetched free slot. WRITE endpoint - has real-world effect (books a real appointment on Optofarm's live system, likely triggers patient notifications).

request_body.patientEmail: string - REQUIRED non-empty. An empty patientEmail makes post_schedule.php return 401 (empty body, no API_ERROR_CUSTOM header) - looks like an auth error but is really a missing-required-field rejection. Confirmed 2026-09-02. A placeholder like noemail@optofarm.ro works fine.
request_body.interventionType: number - index into the calendar's interventiontypes list from get_info.php
request_body.patientid: string, optional (NEW in Postman v4, 2026-09-07) - patientid returned by get_patient.php. If given, the booking is tied DIRECTLY to that existing patient (a real appointment, not a lead/agenda insertion) and patientName, patientEmail, patientPhone are IGNORED. In the v4 collection this field ships disabled by default. Per Imreh's message (HU): 'ha van patientid megadva akkor a patientName, email es phone nem lessz szamitasba veve'.

notes: CORRECTED 2026-08-31 (2nd test, via a real n8n webhook workflow): the original theory that problemDescription must match one of the calendar's predefined options was likely WRONG - it was confounded with a different variable. A follow-up test booked a FRESH free slot on the same calendar (Dr. Baricz Anna / Fortuna) with an arbitrary free-text problemDescription and it succeeded ({"Result":"OK"}). A second call immediately after, using the calendar's exact predefined problemDescription text but reusing the SAME now-already-booked slotid, failed with {"Result":"ERROR","errorcode":1}. This strongly suggests errorcode:1 (at least in that case) simply means 'slot no longer available', not a problemDescription format issue. The real cause of the very first session's errorcode:1 (different calendar: Dr. Ardelean Adina) remains UNCONFIRMED - do not assume problemDescription content is the cause. Ask dRoot Solutions what errorcode 1 (and other errorcodes) actually mean.

interventionType was omitted on all calls (calendar's interventiontypes list from get_info.php was empty, like all 30 calendars in this institution) and booking still succeeded when the slot was free - so interventionType appears optional/ignorable when the calendar defines no intervention types.
IMPORTANT: on success, post_schedule.php's response body contains no scheduleid or other booking identifier - just {"Result":"OK"}.

IMPORTANT: the resulting booking does NOT appear in get_schedule.php's listing (which only returned records in state 'Programat'/confirmed) nor is it findable via get_schedule_patient.php by the phone used - even minutes after creation, across several phone-format variants. This strongly suggests bookings created via this endpoint start in a pending/unconfirmed state that the other thirdpartyai read endpoints do not surface, and that there is currently no known API-only way to retrieve the scheduleid of a just-created booking.

Practical consequence for the n8n/ElevenLabs integration: a voice agent using post_schedule.php cannot immediately confirm/read back/cancel its own booking via this API - staff likely need to confirm it first in the droot/evolvo admin UI before it becomes visible/manageable via get_schedule.php + update_schedule.php. Confirm this behavior with dRoot Solutions (Imreh R.) before relying on it.

v4 (2026-09-07): two booking modes now exist. (a) WITHOUT patientid -> lead/agenda insertion (the old behavior; visible via get_schedule*.php only with schedule_form=0 or 3). (b) WITH patientid from get_patient.php -> appointment attached straight to the existing patient's CRM record; name/email/phone in the request are ignored, so the caller MUST be matched to the right patient (a family can share one phone - match get_patient.php results by name before passing patientid). Whether mode (b) still returns only {Result:OK} without a scheduleid is unverified - check live via get_schedule.php schedule_form=1 right after booking.
